packet.claim: The test campaign expects the response verdict to change when a refusal phrase is added after a fenced JSON object, but the documented rule says the refusal heuristic only decides the verdict when no object can be recovered.
packet.expected: The response verdict remains JSON_OBJECT because the fenced object is recoverable.
packet.observed: The code returned JSON_OBJECT unchanged; the test recorded as_expected false.
packet.scope: Any reply containing a recoverable JSON object and a refusal phrase after it.
packet.source_basis: The refusal heuristic decides the verdict only when no object can be recovered; whether a phrase occurred at all is a separate fact, :func:`refusal_phrase_in`, recorded beside a recovered object (H36: a refusal followed by a form is a refusal and a form).
packet.uncertainty: The second test's mutation was invalid (rewritten text no cell of grammar), so its expectation that recovery moves to a later outside object was not executed; the rule also says fenced objects take priority over later top-level objects.
